C-VV-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-SKILL.Summary: Add the vv-design-principles managed skill: a build-and-audit design process anchored on a project DESIGN.md design-system file, shipped as bundled templates with on-demand references.
C-VV-DESIGN-PRINCIPLES-SKILL.Problem: vv-opencode ships managed skills for the work protocol and vvoc tooling, but nothing covers visual and interaction craft. Coding agents without craft guidance converge on machine-recognizable "AI slop" patterns; research shows generic written encouragement ("be distinctive") can score worse than no guidance, while a subtractive audit pass against a concrete tell catalog reverses it. The package also has no design-system anchor file, so project-specific design decisions have nowhere to live or be checked.

Goals.Goal: Add managed skill vv-design-principles with a compact SKILL.md process: design token plan, build against a measurable quality floor, subtractive slop audit, and deliberate-deviation reporting.
Anchor the skill on a project DESIGN.md: discover it, validate token choices against it, and propose creating or filling it when missing; ship the DESIGN.md contract as an on-demand reference.

Ship the slop-tell catalog and the measurable quality floor as additional on-demand references sourced from public research (Charles Liu's 20 indicators, Anthropic frontend-design defaults, Impeccable, Paralect, Show HN slop scoring).
Register the skill through the existing managed-skills machinery so install, sync, doctor drift reporting, and packed templates cover it without new config surface.

Constraints.Constraint: Skill content is in English, uses YAML frontmatter like other managed templates, and keeps SKILL.md compact with details in on-demand references.

The package surface change is additive only: one MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES entry plus template files. No vvoc schema, plugin, agent, model-role, or config changes; install/sync/doctor coverage follows from the existing loop over managed names.
Existing managed install/sync semantics stay untouched: user-owned skill files keep created/kept/skipped protection, references only sync when the parent skill is not skipped.
Do not modify the user's personal frontend-design skill or any existing bundled vv-* or vvoc-* skill content.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No mechanical slop detector, linter, CI gate, or browser tooling; the catalog is agent guidance, not a code checker.
No optional-skills config list or vvoc schema extension.
No changes to managed agents, the vv-* work-protocol skills, or plugin runtime behavior.
No automatic migration or removal of user-level design skills on any machine.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: vvoc install creates the managed skills directory entry vv-design-principles/SKILL.md plus references slop-tells.md, quality-floor.md, and design-md.md; vvoc sync refreshes them idempotently and preserves user-owned files under the existing rules.

MANAGED_SKILL_NAMES contains vv-design-principles, and install/sync reports plus doctor managed-skill drift warnings cover the new name through the existing loop without code changes outside the registry and tests.

Managed-skills tests assert the registration, frontmatter name and description triggers, discovery of exactly the three references, and stable content anchors for the slop-tell catalog, the quality floor (contrast, type size, line height, measure, focus, targets, reduced motion, real content), and the DESIGN.md contract (discover, validate against, propose creation).
README documents the skill in the managed skills table and the compatibility surface stays truthful; GRACE graph and verification state reflect the new skill inside this change lifecycle.
grace lint --path . passes with the approved bundle and updated durable graph/verification state.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh test output asserts the new skill registration, template frontmatter, the three shipped references, and catalog content anchors; opencode tests cover install/sync/doctor behavior for the new managed name; grace lint reports no errors with the active change bundle and updated graph/verification state.

Assumptions.Assumption: The skill is agent guidance, not executable tooling; runtime behavior changes only through the managed-skill registry entry and its install/sync surface.
vv-design-principles coexists with user-level design skills; the frontmatter description keeps its triggers distinguishable from building/auditing requests that other skills may also claim.
DESIGN.md is a plain markdown file the agent reads and writes in the user's project; the skill defines its contract but vvoc does not lint or manage the file itself.
